claims.statement: LunaNexa is a provider-neutral model and GPU-cluster control plane, not a MoonSuite application or agent runtime.
Managed GPU nodes receive the LunaNexa node agent, approved runtime containers, signed model artifacts, and bounded telemetry—not application repositories or product credentials.
limitations: Live image and runtime-environment scans remain part of physical-cluster acceptance.

claims.statement: The repository implements controller, scheduling, enrollment, registry, workspace authority, deployment operations, Rabbita sites, client transport, and recovery evidence baselines.
limitations: Implementation is not equivalent to real four-node production acceptance.

claims.statement: The four physical DGX Spark fleet has passed complete production acceptance.
limitations: Physical enrollment, real serving, measured performance, live security scans, and named human acceptance are still required.

claims.statement: The local four-node simulator exercises placement, routing, drain, queueing, restart, and leak-check behavior.
limitations: It does not validate NVIDIA hardware, thermal behavior, network topology, container runtime, or service objectives.

claims.statement: PostgreSQL is the production system of record for management authority, including control, registry, enrollment, scheduler, telemetry and deployment snapshots; one elected controller serves while standby processes wait.
limitations: The reference PostgreSQL StatefulSet is development-only and single-instance. Production requires an external HA database; configuration and leadership fencing do not prove deployed replication, failover, backup recovery or zero interruption.

claims.statement: The workbench and VS Code extension invoke generic model workloads under scoped workspace authority without granting a DGX shell.
limitations: Third-party editor handoffs are typed integration points, not bundled vendor runtimes.

claims.statement: A signed catalog template can produce a deterministic plan and durable model-service operation without bypassing preflight policy.
limitations: Real runtime images, model artifacts, routes, and capacity must be qualified on the physical cluster.

claims.statement: The repository contains secret-free single-node DGX Spark qualification manifests for vLLM and SGLang.
limitations: They require real ARM64 image digests, a verified model directory, NVIDIA runtime support, and a production packaging adapter before promotion.

claims.statement: The repository implements durable tenant notifications, actionable operator alerts, bounded structured operational events, low-cardinality metrics and receipt-based audit correlation.
limitations: External email, SMS, webhook, metrics, log and paging destinations remain deployment-owned integrations.

claims.statement: The repository implements a generation-fenced hybrid online/offline order, document, evidence-review and fulfillment workflow with MoonLeaf OOXML verification and renderer-bound release evidence.
limitations: Legal templates, object storage, malware scanning, rendering authority, payment, invoice, seal and retention procedures require named external owners before production use.

claims.statement: The enterprise portal exposes a tenant-safe exclusive-machine lifecycle with opaque credential handoff, coarse reachability, automatic expiry and explicit early termination without exposing physical topology or raw credentials.
limitations: Production IdP, trusted ingress, SSH certificate authority or broker, node-local watchdog and sanitization rehearsal remain required.

claims.statement: The repository includes a LunaNexa-operated Keycloak public identity profile with open registration, verified email, TOTP, exact PKCE clients, digest-pinned images and restricted ingress.
limitations: Real DNS, TLS, SMTP, PostgreSQL failover, identity-gateway image and browser smoke acceptance remain deployment evidence.

claims.statement: The separate coursebook implements a role-protected, read-only administrator diagnostics projection with a versioned skill inventory, bounded live aggregates, stale-index detection, bilingual runbook links and redacted audit evidence.
limitations: Production activation requires the approved identity proxy, matching HMAC secret, internal HTTPS diagnostics gateway and secret-backed controller authority.

claims.statement: The next major-version roadmap separates managed inference from dedicated GPU workspace access and assigns each an independent evidence-based launch gate.
limitations: Neither offering is production-ready until its physical and external acceptance gates pass.

open_gaps: Source digests identify the current working-tree bytes. This refresh includes the parallel undertaking rental admission and cancellation-safe persistence changes; it is not a fresh comprehensive audit of every historical coursebook claim. Undertaking PDF rendering and live object delivery remain unverified. Production evidence separately requires physical deployment and external-adapter acceptance.
No physical DGX Spark node has been exercised by this documentation generation run.
The vLLM/SGLang qualification path uses a separate multi-file model directory; production assignment-bound extraction/packaging still needs review.

Production CA/mTLS, identity-gateway image, platform-identity DNS/TLS/SMTP/PostgreSQL, OCI registry, metrics, secret provider, model license, and named human acceptors remain external deployment inputs.
The optional documentation pet is implemented and locally testable, but a live MoonClaw model route is not claimed until configured and exercised.
Administrator guide diagnostics are implemented and locally contract-tested, but remain disabled until a trusted identity proxy and internal HTTPS diagnostics gateway are configured.
